meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: One of the pathway's major negative feedback loops, and the best studied. Sustained S6K1 activity, as in obesity and nutrient excess, phosphorylates IRS-1 and represses its expression, so the insulin receptor can no longer signal to PI3K. This is a major reason blocking mTORC1 paradoxically RAISES Akt activity (the Grb10 arm adds to it). Rapalog-associated insulin resistance runs mainly through a different route, disruption of mTORC2 (LAM2012, in mice).
data.mechanism_beginner: This is one of the pathway's main self-limiting "off switches": strong, sustained S6K1 activity shuts down IRS-1, cutting the insulin signal off. That is how too much food can blunt the insulin signal. It also runs the other way: block mTOR and IRS-1 survives, so Akt can paradoxically become MORE active – which is why the insulin resistance seen on these drugs is blamed, on evidence from mice, on a different mechanism (loss of mTORC2), not on this loop.
data.boundary: Established in cells and mouse genetics. The size of this arm's contribution to rapalog dysglycaemia in humans, relative to mTORC2 loss, has not been apportioned.
